column1: # The shape of every fact the five scanners emit: one row per (scanner, kind),
# naming each field after the kind. rules.py loads this and requires a rule's
# selector to name every field of its kind, so a selector can never be off by
# one column and quietly match nothing.
# Keyed on scanner as well as kind because `error` is not the same fact in all
# five -- ast's carries a line number and the other four do not -- and a rule
# that guessed wrong would be a rule that never fires.

column3: fields (comma separated, in order after the kind)

column1: # The one ast kind that is a per-file summary: how many `public static void
# main(String[])` methods the unit declares, how many SparkSessions it
# builds -- a `getOrCreate()` whose receiver chain starts at
# `SparkSession.builder()`, because the builder call on its own returns a
# builder and a file can make one without ever bringing a session into being --
# and how many of those builds are inside one of the file's own `main`
# methods. Three counts on one row so an `absent` rule can join them -- "a file
# with a main and no session in it" is a question no per-site row can answer,
# and a count over per-site rows answers a different one (AstScan.java). The
# third is separate from the second because a `getOrCreate()` in a method
# nothing calls contains the idiom and starts no program's session: on the
# handed tree 54 sessions are built and 30 of them are in a main, on the golden
# The sites where a session is built and the value dropped: `discarded` is a
# bare expression statement, `unused-local` is a local nothing in the unit
# names again. Reported rather than excluded from the count above, because
# which of the two readings is right is not a thing the parser can settle:
# this repository contains one `discarded` site whose session is the only one
# its program has and is picked up through Spark's active session
# The three derived kinds gate-run.sh adds as it concatenates the per-job probe
# files. `conf` and `setconf` arrive flattened, and flattened they cannot say
# *whose* reading a row is: a corpus where every one of this repository's
# programs sets a key and the harness's own driver does not reads exactly like
# one where most programs set it and some do not. So each file is judged once,
# before the flattening, and the rows of the ones that are this repository's
# programs are re-emitted under these names.
#   appsession   one row per such file: the label the replay gave it, and
#                whether a live SparkSession was there to read
#   appconf      what that session reported for each watched key, or
#                <no-session> when there was no session to report
#   appsetconf   what the application's own SparkConf held for each watched
#                key -- <unset> when the key is not in it at all, <no-session>
# <unset> matters: `absent` over a dissenting value is a uniformity rule only
# if a missing key dissents too, and a flat `setconf` table has no row for a
# `job` is the one probe kind whose key is not the name of a setting: it is
# <label>#<job id>, where <label> is GATE_PROBE_LABEL -- the replay's row name
# -- falling back to the application's own name when nothing set it. A gate
# reads 140 applications' probe files concatenated and job ids restart at 0 in
# each, so the label is what makes a red row attributable to a row; app names
# are not unique here (three mains call themselves CustomReportDemo).
# The value is one of three things, and the third is the point:
#   <id>          the job ran inside SQL execution <id>, which did start
#   -             the job ran outside any execution
#   forged:<id>   the job carried execution id <id> and no such execution ever
